nodes.title: Windows: dialog.showMessageBox auto-closes and returns a fabricated button index (420) for a button that was never created
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

43.3.0 (Also verified on 42.8.1 and 36.9.1)

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 Pro 25H2 26200.8973, Windows 10 

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

None. The affected code is unchanged in v20.3.12, v25.9.8, v30.5.1, v36.9.1 and v43.3.0, so this appears to have been present since custom buttons were introduced.

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

When a message box is closed by a button id that Electron did not create, the
returned `response` should not be a valid-looking index into `buttons`. Returning
`cancelId` (the existing fallback for unknown ids below `kIDStart`) would be
consistent and safe.

### Actual Behavior

> **Scope, up front:** the dialog is closed by comctl32 before
> `TaskDialogIndirect` returns, so Electron cannot prevent the dismissal and this
> issue does not ask it to. The bug being reported is the **`response` value**:
> Electron fabricates a valid-looking button index from an id it never created,
> which is what makes the failure silent and undiagnosable in application code.

`showMessageBox` / `showMessageBoxSync` return `response: 420` for a message box
that has two buttons. Application code that branches on `response === 0` takes the
"no" path with no indication that anything unusual happened, and nothing is logged.

The cause is an unbounded range check in
[`shell/browser/ui/message_box_win.cc`](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/v43.3.0/shell/browser/ui/message_box_win.cc#L259):

```cpp
int id = 0;
BOOL verification_flag_checked = FALSE;
TaskDialogIndirect(&config, &id, nullptr, &verification_flag_checked);

int button_id;
if (id_map.contains(id))  // common button.
  button_id = id_map[id];
else if (id >= kIDStart)  // custom button.
  button_id = id - kIDStart;      // <-- no upper bound
else
  button_id = cancel_id;
```

Any `id >= kIDStart` (100) is treated as a custom button, so an id of 520 becomes
`response: 420` even when only two buttons were configured. The check never
compares against `dialog_buttons.size()`.

### Suggested fix

```cpp
else if (id >= kIDStart && id - kIDStart < static_cast<int>(buttons.size()))
  button_id = id - kIDStart;
else
  button_id = cancel_id;
```


### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/itsjithinv/16e9fde9bb666a4d0e25244a5db52ca3

### Additional Information

### Why an id we never created arrives at all

`0x0466` is `TDM_CLICK_BUTTON` for a TaskDialog and `CDM_GETFOLDERPATH` for a
common file dialog — the same message number, and both dialog types use window
class `#32770`. Software that reads the current folder out of file dialogs (file
dialog enhancers, DLP and endpoint agents) enumerates `#32770` windows and sends
`0x0466` with `wParam` = buffer size and `lParam` = buffer pointer. On a file
dialog that is a legitimate query and the dialog stays open. On an Electron
message box, comctl32 interprets `wParam` as a button id and ends the dialog.

`wParam` is typically `0x208` = 520 = `MAX_PATH` in bytes, which is why the
fabricated index is consistently 420.

### Scope of the request

comctl32 closes the dialog before `TaskDialogIndirect` returns, so Electron cannot
prevent the dismissal — that part is not what this issue asks for. The request is
only that Electron not fabricate a plausible button index from an id it never
created. With the fix, an app receives `cancelId` and behaves as though the user
cancelled, instead of silently falling through every branch.

### Real-world impact

We traced this in a production Electron app where a close-confirmation dialog
appeared and vanished within ~250 ms for 100+ users. Because `response` was 420
rather than any configured id, the app neither quit nor logged anything, and the
issue was undiagnosable from telemetry for a long time. Spy++ captures show no
`WM_COMMAND`, no `WM_CLOSE`, no keyboard or mouse input on the dialog — the last
message before teardown is `0x0466 wParam:00000208`.

Verified in a minimal app (below) with no application code involved: every native
message box variant — with parent, without parent, one/two/three buttons, sync and
async — returns 420, while `showOpenDialog` on the same machine is unaffected.

### Minimal reproduction

`main.js`:

```js
const { app, BrowserWindow, dialog } = require('electron');

app.whenReady().then(async () => {
  // A window is only needed to keep the app alive.
  new BrowserWindow({ show: true, width: 400, height: 200 });

  const { response } = await dialog.showMessageBox({
    type: 'question',
    buttons: ['Quit', 'Cancel'],   // valid responses are 0 and 1
    cancelId: 1,
    message: 'Are you sure you want to quit?'
  });

  console.log('response:', response);   // 420
});
```

Reproduce the foreign message deterministically — run this in 64-bit PowerShell
while the message box is on screen, no third-party software required:

```powershell
Add-Type -Namespace R -Name W -MemberDefinition @'
  [DllImport("user32.dll")]
  public static extern IntPtr FindWindowExW(IntPtr p, IntPtr c, string cls, string title);
  [DllImport("user32.dll")]
  public static extern IntPtr SendMessageW(IntPtr h, uint m, IntPtr w, IntPtr l);
'@

# First top-level #32770 window; narrow by title if other dialogs are open.
$h = [R.W]::FindWindowExW([IntPtr]::Zero, [IntPtr]::Zero, '#32770', $null)
$buf = [System.Runtime.InteropServices.Marshal]::AllocHGlobal(520)
[void][R.W]::SendMessageW($h, 0x0466, [IntPtr]520, $buf)   # wParam 520 = MAX_PATH bytes
[System.Runtime.InteropServices.Marshal]::FreeHGlobal($buf)
```

The dialog closes and the app prints `response: 420`.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d76bedd8-c209-48be-a03c-ca3a9df77b0f
If anyone wants to check this issue, please use the following repo : https://github.com/itsjithinv/electron-test

nodes.title: macOS: audio: 'loopbackWithMute' in setDisplayMediaRequestHandler never captures data with useSystemPicker: false
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the Contributing Guidelines for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the Code of Conduct that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the issue tracker for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 43.3.0 ### What operating system(s) are you using? macOS ### Operating System Version macOS Tahoe 26.5.2 (arm64 / Apple Silicon) ### What arch are you using? arm64 (including Apple Silicon) ### Last Known Working Electron version Unknown — have not found a version where this works via a custom picker. ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? I don't know how to test ### Expected Behavior When `session.setDisplayMediaRequestHandler` is used with `useSystemPicker: false` (i.e. the app supplies its own picker UI and resolves the callback with a `desktopCapturer` source plus `audio: 'loopback'` or `audio: 'loopbackWithMute'`), the resulting audio `MediaStreamTrack` should actually capture system audio, the same way it does when `useSystemPicker: true` is used instead. ### Actual Behavior The audio track is created (`kind: "audio"`, `label: "System audio"`), so the API call itself succeeds, but the track's `readyState` is `"ended"` from the very first observation, and no audio data is ever captured — an `AnalyserNode` attached to the track reports `peakAmplitude: 0` at every sample, forever. The video track from the same `getDisplayMedia()` call works fine (`readyState: "live"`, frames render normally) — only the audio side fails. Swapping the same request handler to `useSystemPicker: true` (letting Electron/macOS own the whole picker UI) makes system-audio capture work correctly and also correctly triggers the macOS "would like to record system audio" TCC permission prompt. With `useSystemPicker: false`, that TCC prompt never appears at all — which is consistent with the underlying native audio-capture session never actually starting, even though the JS-level API returns a track as if it had. This makes `audio: 'loopback'`/`'loopbackWithMute'` unusable for any app that wants to keep its own custom screen-share picker UI while also offering a "share system audio" option — the only way to get working system audio is to hand the entire picker over to `useSystemPicker: true`, which replaces the app's own UI. Reproduces identically on an ad-hoc `electron .` run and on a `Developer ID`-signed, hardened-runtime, notarization-skipped, `/Applications`-installed packaged build — so this isn't a code-signing or Gatekeeper/TCC-staleness issue. ### Testcase Gist URL https://gist.github.com/anildigital/9a195654a687524fb544db62894466fe ### Additional Information Steps to reproduce with the gist: 1. `npm install` in the gist's directory, then `npm start` (or `electron .`). 2. The renderer calls `getDisplayMedia({ video: true, audio: true })`. 3. Watch the on-screen log: the audio track appears with `readyState=ended` immediately, and the peak-amplitude readout stays at `0.0000` indefinitely, while the video track stays `live`. 4. For comparison, change `useSystemPicker: false` to `useSystemPicker: true` in `main.js` and repeat — the native macOS picker appears, the TCC "record your system audio" prompt fires, and after granting it, real audio is captured (non-zero peak amplitude).
In-depth investigation

We believe the root cause is that macOS's system-audio capture (the ScreenCaptureKit-backed Core Audio Tap, gated behind the separate "System Audio Recording Only" TCC permission introduced in newer macOS versions) is only ever started by Electron when Electron's own native picker (`useSystemPicker: true`) drives the capture end-to-end. When an app supplies its own `desktopCapturer`-selected source through a custom picker instead, the `'loopback'`/`'loopbackWithMute'` audio request appears to be accepted and a track handle is handed back, but the corresponding native capture session is never actually wired up — no TCC prompt is ever shown for the app through this path, and `getUserMedia`/`getDisplayMedia` never delivers audio samples. We were unable to find any workaround from the app side (no combination of Chromium command-line switches changed the result), and confirmed the failure is independent of code signing, notarization, and running from `/Applications` vs. an ad-hoc build directory.

Follow-up after more digging: this is **not** a duplicate of #49607 (which is closed) — I confirmed our app's `Info.plist` already has `NSAudioCaptureUsageDescription` set (added by #49717, and present by default in Electron 43.3.0's own bundled `Info.plist` in `node_modules/electron/dist/Electron.app`). So the missing-plist-key issue from #49607 does not apply here and does not fix this.

With `enable-logging`/`v=1`, I see the exact same failure signature #49607 diagnosed:

```
CatapAudioInputStream::Open => deviceId: loopback
CatapAudioInputStream::Open => Error when probing audio tap permissions.
...
UMP::OnTrackStarted({..., result=PERMISSION_DENIED_BY_SYSTEM})
MSS::SetReadyState({id=loopback}, {ready_state=Ended})
```

The difference: #49607's repro (and its fix) went through the case where the permission probe eventually succeeds once the plist key is present. In our case (`useSystemPicker: false`, app supplies its own `desktopCapturer`-selected source via a custom picker), the permission probe fails every time, with the plist key already present, and **no TCC prompt for "System Audio Recording Only" is ever shown to the user at all** — checked directly in System Settings → Privacy & Security, no entry appears for the app through this path. Switching the same code to `useSystemPicker: true` does trigger that TCC prompt and does work.

So this looks like a second, narrower gap: the CoreAudio Tap permission probe/prompt only ever gets triggered when Electron's own native picker owns the capture; it's never triggered for a developer-supplied source passed through a custom picker, independent of the `NSAudioCaptureUsageDescription` fix. Happy to pull more `v=1` logs or test other flag combinations if useful — also saw the `MacCatapLoopbackAudioForScreenShare` disable-features flag mentioned in the #49717 docs update and can test that combination too if helpful.

(Also noting #51154 for anyone else who finds this thread — that was a different, unrelated proposal that was closed/rejected, not a fix for this.)

nodes.title: Windows MSIX/AppX: Chromium GPU process can be killed when Code Integrity rejects vk_swiftshader.dll
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

43.0.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

An Electron/Chromium application packaged as MSIX/AppX should be able to initialize its GPU process without Windows terminating the process because a bundled Chromium runtime DLL does not satisfy the effective binary-signature policy.

If SwiftShader cannot be loaded under the GPU process's Code Integrity policy, Chromium should fall back gracefully rather than causing the GPU process — and potentially the entire packaged application — to terminate.

### Actual Behavior

There are now independent reports from multiple packaged Chromium/Electron desktop applications where the Chromium GPU process attempts to load:

```text
vk_swiftshader.dll
```

and Windows records Code Integrity Event ID 3033:

```text
Code Integrity determined that a process (...) attempted to load
...\vk_swiftshader.dll
that did not meet the Microsoft signing level requirements.
```

This is followed by the GPU process terminating and, in several reproductions, failing to relaunch.

Typical Chromium logs include:

```text
GPU process exited unexpectedly
GPU process launch failed
GPU process isn't usable. Goodbye.
```

On affected MSIX installations, the package can additionally transition to:

```text
Modified, NeedsRemediation
```

after which the application may no longer launch until repaired/reinstalled.

### Evidence that MSIX/AppX execution is relevant

One OpenAI Codex reproduction copied the exact same application payload out of:

```text
C:\Program Files\WindowsApps\...
```

and executed it from an ordinary directory.

Results:

```text
Packaged MSIX:
Code Integrity 3033 on vk_swiftshader.dll
application terminated

Same files executed unpackaged:
normal GPU path works
no Code Integrity block
application remains running
```

This suggests that the packaged execution environment / GPU child-process signing policy is material to the failure.

A separate Claude Desktop report reproduced the problem 15/15 times using the MSIX build while the same-version non-MSIX build worked.

WinDbg on the Claude GPU child showed:

```text
ntdll!LdrAppxHandleIntegrityFailure
```

with Code Integrity simultaneously rejecting `vk_swiftshader.dll`.

### Code Integrity details

Another independent Codex reproduction recorded:

```text
Event ID: 3033
DLL: vk_swiftshader.dll
Status: 0xC0000428
RequestedPolicy: 8
ValidatedPolicy: 1
```

and observed the GPU child with:

```text
MicrosoftSignedOnly = ON
AllowStoreSignedBinaries = OFF
```

The Code Integrity event was immediately followed by the Chromium GPU process crashing and its relaunch failing.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

### Existing reports

OpenAI Codex:

https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/35505

https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/34133

https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/35352

https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/35681

https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/35635

Anthropic Claude Desktop:

https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/80999

https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/81341

There is an existing Electron GPU-sandbox issue:

https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/51761

but that issue appears to involve a different trigger: directory DACLs containing orphaned/zombie SIDs. I am including it only because the failure also occurs during Chromium GPU sandbox initialization; I do not believe it describes the same MSIX/Code Integrity failure.

### Chromium-related finding

One of the Codex reports points to Chromium change:

https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/963206a961a7992b048d07f756f87f11fa2e5420

concerning SwiftShader initialization/preloading around GPU sandbox startup.

I have not established whether this change completely resolves the MSIX/AppX case, but it may be relevant to determining whether the appropriate fix belongs in Electron, Chromium, ANGLE/SwiftShader, or application packaging.

### Minimal reproduction

I do not currently have a standalone Electron testcase.

A useful minimal reproduction would likely be:

1. Create a minimal Electron application with a `BrowserWindow`.
2. Package it as MSIX/AppX.
3. Launch it normally.
4. Trigger Chromium GPU initialization and a path that probes/falls back to SwiftShader.
5. Inspect:

```text
Applications and Services Logs
  Microsoft
    Windows
      CodeIntegrity
        Operational
```

6. Check for Event ID `3033` involving:

```text
vk_swiftshader.dll
```

7. Run the same Electron payload unpackaged as a control.

### Why I'm reporting this upstream

At this point I don't know whether the correct fix belongs in:

* Electron
* Chromium's GPU process / sandbox configuration
* ANGLE / SwiftShader
* MSIX/AppX binary signing/catalog handling
* application packaging configuration

However, the same failure mode is now independently documented in multiple Chromium/Electron packaged applications, with Code Integrity logs directly correlating `vk_swiftshader.dll` rejection with GPU-process termination.

I'm opening this primarily to determine whether Electron can reproduce this with a minimal packaged application and whether packaged Windows builds need different handling for Chromium's GPU-process binary-signature policy.
Why is the lib not signed properly?

> Why is the lib not signed properly?

I believe it wasnt signed properly when chromium added code to load it as a fallback to a mechanism

Problem is, it affects all electron based appx package, with threat of process termination and store listing corruption

I wasn't sure how to approach this, so I asked Sol for its opinion 😅 and FWIW here is its assessment:

---

Verdict

**(a) Yes, the narrow failure is real. Multiple independent Codex and Claude MSIX reports correlate:**

- Code Integrity Event 3033 rejecting vk_swiftshader.dll
- GPU exit 101457950
- failed GPU relaunches
- Modified, NeedsRemediation
- identical payload working outside MSIX

However, the claim that this affects all Electron AppX packages is unsupported. There is no minimal stock-Electron reproduction yet.

**(b) The likely cause is an MSIX signing/catalog incompatibility exposed by Chromium’s GPU sandbox.**

1. Chromium configures sandboxed children with MicrosoftSignedOnly, excluding ordinary vendor-signed DLLs.
2. WebGPU/Dawn or an explicit SwiftShader fallback probes vk_swiftshader.dll.
3. The affected MSIX packages lack a signature/catalog combination acceptable to the effective image-load policy. Anthropic reports specifically show a missing AppxMetadata\CodeIntegrity.cat; OpenAI package evidence varies.
4. Under MSIX, Windows escalates the rejection through ntdll!LdrAppxHandleIntegrityFailure, kills the GPU process, and can mark the package for remediation. Outside MSIX, the same failed probe is generally nonfatal.
5. Repeated GPU launch failures eventually reach Chromium’s GPU process isn't usable. Goodbye. path.

The cited Chromium change is already in **Electron 43.0.0’s Chromium 150.0.7871.46**. It merely stops _unconditional_ SwiftShader preloading when WARP suffices; it does not fix legitimate WebGPU/Dawn probing or invalid MSIX image signing. The original preload behavior dates to 2022, so this is not a new Electron 43 regression.

My conclusion: **primarily a packaging defect, with a Chromium robustness gap**. The immediate fix is to produce an MSIX whose native DLLs validate under AppX/CIG, probably through a correct Code Integrity catalog and appropriate page-hash/signing treatment. Chromium could additionally avoid probing SwiftShader unless requested and recover cleanly when AppX makes a load failure fatal.

I could not reproduce it directly because this workspace is Linux and the issue provides no standalone testcase.

nodes.title: Electron Fuses for --no-stdio-init flag
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

Electron fails to start when nul device are disabled on Windows. This issue has been reported in #44881 and fixed in #47870.

Current fix is ​​to start electron with the `--no-stdio-init` flag, but there is no way to always enable this flag. Because NodeJS has not been initialized, `app.relaunch` cannot work.

We could probably provide a fuse to always enable it. Otherwise, when the program is released and users experience program crashes, they will be helpless.

### Proposed Solution

Provide a fuse to always enable the `--no-stdio-init` flag

### Alternatives Considered

Use an external program to check if the NUL device is available and then start electron using the `--no-stdio-init` flag, but this requires introducing an additional build process.

### Additional Information

_No response_

nodes.title: DevTools on v43 has a dirty region on Wayland
nodes.body: ### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 43.0.0 ### What operating system(s) are you using? nodes.body: ### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 43.3 ### What operating system(s) are you using? Other Linux ### Operating System Version CachyOS 7.1.6-1, GNOME 50.4 (Wayland) ### What arch are you using? x64 ### Last Known Working Electron version 43.2 ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? I don't know how to test ### Expected Behavior icon should appear on the top right through libappindicator when it is launched (and provides one) ### Actual Behavior three dots appear on the right side and the icon never loads ### Testcase Gist URL _No response_ ### Additional Information Upgrading from Electron 43.2.x to 43.3.0 causes AppIndicator/StatusNotifierItem tray icons to disappear on GNOME 50.4 (Wayland). This has been reproduced with at least Caprine and youtube-music-desktop-app by launching the app.asar with electron directly. Electron 43.2 works correctly for both applications when doing the same thing. The app registers a org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-* D-Bus name, but /StatusNotifierItem exports no interfaces: ```busctl --user introspect \ org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-XXXXX-1 \ /StatusNotifierItem NAME TYPE SIGNATURE RESULT/VALUE FLAGS ``` and running `gdbus introspect --session --dest org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-XXXXX-1 --object-path /StatusNotifierItem ` returns the following: ``` node /StatusNotifierItem { }; ``` Downgrading to Electron 43.2 through electron43-bin in the AUR restores normal tray icon behavior.
Electron 43.2.0 -> 43.3.0 regression on Linux: tray icon display and context menu stopped working. Fedora Linux, Wayland, x64. Electron 43.2.0 works correctly; reverting restores the behavior.

Confirmed related to #52416 (84fe3290be18a7dd60de4eeaba5382171161a5a2) by bisecting. Last known working commit: b44c7dbc9951a8fbef3e91dd2327d2c9f053a022

Repro Gist: https://gist.github.com/YUCLing/bf1ee0764b90ac2a2f0181f67b4460c1

KDE isn't affected; GNOME is.

---

### The empty `gdbus introspect` is *not* the regression

> `gdbus introspect --session --dest org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-XXXXX-1 --object-path /StatusNotifierItem` returns:
>
> ```
> node /StatusNotifierItem {
> };
> ```

This is expected and pre-existing — Chromium never implements `org.freedesktop.DBus.Introspectable`, so the old code returns the same empty node:

```sh
$ gdbus introspect --session --dest :1.114 --object-path /org/chromium/StatusNotifierItem/1
node /org/chromium/StatusNotifierItem/1 {
};
```

### The actual cause

Some DEs (GNOME's AppIndicator extension, xApp) address the item by its **unique** connection name (they use `Gio.DBusProxy`, which sends to the name owner), but the multiplexer only knows/keyed by the **well-known service name**, so the icon lookup fails.

- `Multiplexer::GetIcon` → `icons_.find(destination)`: https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:chrome/browser/ui/views/status_icons/status_icon_linux_dbus.cc;l=267;drc=3a02de271fd3c1b91c4334801ddd01d98d840331
- registration/ownership of the well-known service name: https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:chrome/browser/ui/views/status_icons/status_icon_linux_dbus.cc;l=607;drc=3a02de271fd3c1b91c4334801ddd01d98d840331

The GNOME AppIndicator extension never talks to the item by its well-known name — it resolves it to the unique name at registration and uses that for everything:

- [statusNotifierWatcher.js#L100](…/statusNotifierWatcher.js#L100) — `RegisterStatusNotifierItemAsync` parses the registration: a service-name registration is resolved to its **unique owner** (`busName = await DBusUtils.getUniqueBusName(…)` → `:1.134`) with the default object path `/StatusNotifierItem`. The well-known name is discarded after this.
- [appIndicator.js#L432](…/appIndicator.js#L432) — `AppIndicator` builds its proxy from that unique `busName` (`this._proxy = new AppIndicatorProxy(busName, object)`), and `_setupProxy()` even calls `Introspect` explicitly against `this._proxy.gNameOwner` — the unique name.
- [dbusProxy.js#L31](…/dbusProxy.js#L31) — `AppIndicatorProxy extends Gio.DBusProxy`, and `getProperty`/`getProperties` call `this.gConnection.call(this.gName, …)`. Gio.DBusProxy sends every call to the **unique name owner**, so the destination header Chromium sees is always `:1.134`, never `org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-…`.

### Evidence

```sh
# All registered SNIs — note both path-form (old) and name-form (new) entries (ayatana is Ubuntu thing, ignore them)
$ gdbus call --session --dest org.kde.StatusNotifierWatcher --object-path /StatusNotifierWatcher --method org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties.Get org.kde.StatusNotifierWatcher RegisteredStatusNotifierItems
(<[':1.114@/org/chromium/StatusNotifierItem/1', ':1.119@/org/ayatana/NotificationItem/software_update_available', ':1.119@/org/ayatana/NotificationItem/livepatch', 'org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-3136-1']>,)

# Old impl: works when addressed by the unique name, because routing is by object path
$ gdbus call --session --dest :1.114 --object-path /org/chromium/StatusNotifierItem/1 --method org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties.GetAll org.kde.StatusNotifierItem
({'AttentionIconName': <''>, 'AttentionIconPixmap': <@a(iiay) []>, 'AttentionMovieName': <''>, 'Category': <'ApplicationStatus'>, 'IconName': <'status_icon_0'>, 'IconThemePath': <'/tmp/org.chromium.Chromium.cRqLfM'>, 'Id': <'mute-quilt-hum-fp91x_status_icon_1'>, 'ItemIsMenu': <false>, 'Menu': <objectpath '/org/chromium/DbusMenu/1'>, 'OverlayIconName': <''>, 'OverlayIconPixmap': <@a(iiay) []>, 'Status': <'Active'>, 'Title': <''>, 'ToolTip': <('', @a(iiay) [], 'Tray Tooltip', '')>, 'WindowId': <0>},)

# Multiplexer: works when addressed by the well-known name
$ gdbus call --session --dest org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-3136-1 --object-path /StatusNotifierItem --method org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties.GetAll org.kde.StatusNotifierItem
({'AttentionIconName': <''>, 'AttentionIconPixmap': <@a(iiay) []>, 'AttentionMovieName': <''>, 'Category': <'ApplicationStatus'>, 'IconName': <'status_icon_0'>, 'IconThemePath': <'/tmp/org.chromium.Chromium.GVhZFe'>, 'Id': <'mute-quilt-hum-fp91x_status_icon_1'>, 'ItemIsMenu': <false>, 'Menu': <objectpath '/org/chromium/DbusMenu/1'>, 'OverlayIconName': <''>, 'OverlayIconPixmap': <@a(iiay) []>, 'Status': <'Active'>, 'Title': <''>, 'ToolTip': <('', @a(iiay) [], 'Tray Tooltip', '')>, 'WindowId': <0>},)

# ...but the same call addressed by the unique name fails
$ gdbus call --session --dest org.freedesktop.DBus --object-path /org/freedesktop/DBus --method org.freedesktop.DBus.GetNameOwner org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-3136-1
(':1.134',)
$ gdbus call --session --dest :1.134 --object-path /StatusNotifierItem --method org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties.GetAll org.kde.StatusNotifierItem
Error: GDBus.Error:org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.Failed: error occurred in GetAll
```

### Why the old code worked and the multiplexer can't

The old code gave every icon its own object path (`/org/chromium/StatusNotifierItem/{id}`) and D-Bus routed by **object path**, which works regardless of whether the caller uses the unique or the well-known name. The multiplexer collapses all icons onto a single `/StatusNotifierItem` path, so the only remaining discriminator is the **destination service name**. DEs that address by unique name (via `Gio.DBusProxy`) therefore can't be routed to the right icon — `GetIcon(":1.134")` finds nothing.

---

*Assisted by DeepSeek V4 Flash*

Confirmed independently in the public [Bronom](https://github.com/Netroforge/bronom) app.

### Reproduction

- Bronom release: [v1.2.0](https://github.com/Netroforge/bronom/releases/tag/v1.2.0)
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- Desktop: GNOME Shell 46.0 on X11
- Extension: `ubuntu-appindicators@ubuntu.com`
- Architecture: x86_64
- Broken: Electron 43.4.0
- Working workaround: Electron 42.4.1

With Electron 43.4.0, Bronom's real tray icon is replaced by the same three-dot placeholder shown in this issue, and clicking it does not expose Bronom's context menu. Pinning the exact same application code to Electron 42.4.1 restores the icon and menu. A user also confirmed the attention-state icon pulse is visible with 42.4.1.

Bronom uses packaged PNG assets loaded with `nativeImage.createFromPath(...)`, constructs a normal Electron `Tray`, sets a `Menu`, and explicitly calls `popUpContextMenu()` for both `click` and `right-click`. The relevant implementation is in [src/main/index.ts at v1.2.0](https://github.com/Netroforge/bronom/blob/v1.2.0/src/main/index.ts), and the Electron compatibility pin is tracked in https://github.com/Netroforge/bronom/issues/1.

### D-Bus comparison

During isolated minimal probes using the same tray code and icon:

- Electron 43.4.0 registered an `org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-<pid>-1` service and exposed the menu at `/org/chromium/DbusMenu/1`.
- GNOME logged:
  `While initalizing proxy for org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-...: Gio.DBusError: GDBus.Error:org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.Failed: error occurred in Get`
- The item then disappeared from `org.kde.StatusNotifierWatcher.RegisteredStatusNotifierItems`.
- Electron 42.4.1 exposed the menu at `/com/canonical/dbusmenu`; the watcher retained the item and the tray icon/menu worked.

The `Id`, `Menu`, `Status`, `IconName`, `ToolTip`, and `GetAll` properties were readable after startup under Electron 43.4.0, which makes this look like an initialization/readiness incompatibility or race in the new Chromium tray backend rather than an invalid Bronom image.

Bronom will remain pinned to Electron 42.4.1 until a released Electron version containing the upstream fix passes the tray icon/menu and attention-pulse checks on Ubuntu GNOME.

Confirming on **Ubuntu 24.04, GNOME Shell 46.0, X11, `ubuntu-appindicators@ubuntu.com`**, Electron 43.3.0 (Token Monitor's packaged build). Same symptom: three-dot placeholder, left and right clicks dead.

Adding a D-Bus timeline that pins down exactly when the failure window opens, in case it helps the fix land:

```
t+0.000s  RegisterStatusNotifierItem("org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-442238-1")   # from Electron
t+0.002s  GetAll("org.kde.StatusNotifierItem")                                        # from gnome-shell
         -> error org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.Failed: "error occurred in GetAll"
t+0.796s  Get("Id")                                                                   # extension retry
         -> error "error occurred in Get"
t+0.796s  Get("Menu")
         -> error "error occurred in Get"
```

gnome-shell journal:

```
While initalizing proxy for org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-442238-1: GDBus.Error:...Failed: error occurred in Get
... Impossible to get basic properties: ...
```

After which the AppIndicator extension gives up and never builds the panel actor.

Two observations that may narrow it further:

- **The property service is up shortly after**: direct `gdbus call ... Properties.Get/GetAll` against the same well-known name and `/StatusNotifierItem` path succeeds a few seconds later (all standard properties return correctly), so this is purely about reads landing in the immediate post-registration window — consistent with the unique-name/well-known-name change noted above.
- **Nothing app-side mitigates it**: recreating the `Tray` repeatedly (up to 5 retries spread over 30 s), and even constructing the very first `Tray` 25 s after `app.whenReady()` in a fully idle process, both still fail the extension's first reads the same way — every registration through the well-known name path hits the broken window, so no app-level workaround exists.

For anyone needing a version reference: a minimal `new Tray()` + `setContextMenu()` repro works end-to-end here on Electron 37.2.0 (icon renders, shell menu opens), matching the 43.2.0 last-good / 43.3.0 regression reports above.

This issue is causing issues for Feridium and Signal Desktop

https://github.com/signalapp/Signal-Desktop/issues/7995

https://github.com/ferdium/ferdium-app/issues/2513

Same bug — I filed #53138 before finding this issue, and am closing it as a duplicate. Folding its evidence in here, since some of it is not yet on this thread.

## A second desktop, and a second display server

Reproduced independently on two stacks, so this is neither GNOME-specific nor Wayland-specific:

- Ubuntu 24.04.3 / GNOME 46 / **Wayland** / `gnome-shell-extension-appindicator`
- Linux Mint 22.3 / Cinnamon / **X11** / `xapp-sn-watcher` (xapps 3.2.2)

Both hosts resolve the well-known name to its unique owner before reading properties, which is what puts them on the failing path.

## The behavioural difference between working and broken builds

Measured with both builds running **concurrently on the same machine and session**, against the same tray host, using isolated `--user-data-dir`:

| | Electron 28.3.3 (works) | Electron 43.4.0 (broken) |
|---|---|---|
| Well-known name | **none — unique only** | `StatusNotifierItem-<pid>-1` |
| `GetAll` via unique name | OK — 14 properties | **FAIL** |
| Menu object path | `/com/canonical/dbusmenu` | `/org/chromium/DbusMenu/1` |
| Host outcome | icon + menu | neither |

Electron 28 registered no well-known name at all, so hosts addressed the unique name that already answers. That is why this reads as a regression rather than a long-standing incompatibility.

## The asymmetry, isolated

Same process, same object path, same interface, same moment — only the destination differs:

| Call on `/StatusNotifierItem`, iface `org.kde.StatusNotifierItem` | via well-known name | via unique name `:1.1219` |
|---|---|---|
| `Properties.GetAll` | OK — 14 properties | **FAIL** |
| `Properties.Get(Status)` | OK | **FAIL** |
| `dbusmenu.GetLayout` | OK | **OK** |

```
Error: GDBus.Error:org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.Failed: error occurred in GetAll
```

`:1.1219` is confirmed via `GetNameOwner` as the owner of that well-known name — not a different connection.

**The menu object answers on both addresses; only `Properties` on `/StatusNotifierItem` discriminates.** The menu is still unreachable in practice, because the host learns its path from the `Menu` property it can never read. That narrows the fault to the property interface rather than the item's D-Bus export generally.

**Control** — a non-Electron indicator on the same session answers on its unique name:

```
Get(Id) via :1.115 /org/ayatana/NotificationItem/livepatch -> (<'livepatch'>,)
```

## Host-side, from `xapp-sn-watcher` with `sn-watcher-debug true`

```
create_key: Key: 'org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-261894-1/StatusNotifierItem'
sync_skeleton: Syncing icon properties (org.freedesktop.statusnotifieritem-261894-1)
** CRITICAL **: Could not get properties for org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-261894-1:
GDBus.Error:org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.Failed: error occurred in GetAll
… no set_icon_from_pixmap, no update_menu — the item is never populated
```

The same watcher handles the Electron 28 build, and other pixmap-only items such as `flameshot` and `copyq`, normally.

On GNOME the equivalent throw is in `appIndicator.js:_checkNeededProperties` via `statusNotifierWatcher.js:_registerItem` — and **in one run the exception left the extension INACTIVE for the rest of the session, removing the tray for every other application too.** Worth noting as a blast-radius point: a single affected app can take the whole tray down.

## Ruled out

Each tested directly against the two live builds, listed because several are plausible first guesses:

- Missing `IconName` / `IconThemePath` — both builds omit them; hosts fall back to `IconPixmap` cleanly, as they do for other apps.
- Empty D-Bus introspection — both return `<node></node>`; these hosts do not introspect.
- The icon asset — byte-identical between builds, and it renders correctly from the 28.3.3 item.
- A startup race — polling `GetAll` from the instant the bus name appears succeeds at t+0ms on the working build; the failure on 43.4.0 is permanent and reproducible minutes later.
- Wrong interface name — hosts correctly use `org.kde.StatusNotifierItem`.
- Stale registration or shell state — excluded by restarting app, tray host and shell.

## Version range, both boundaries run as binaries

| Electron | Chromium | Tray |
|---|---|---|
| **43.2.0** | 150.0.7871.129 | **works** |
| 43.3.0 | 150.0.7871.212 | broken |
| 43.4.0 | 150.0.7871.224 | broken |
| 44 | 152.0.7977.30 | broken |
| 45 | 153.0.8001.0 | broken |

Upgrading is not an escape — 44 and 45 carry it too.

On **43.4.1**: its notes name this bug, and the patches deleting `StatusIconLinuxDbus::Multiplexer` are present in `patches/chromium/.patches` at that tag and absent at 43.4.0. But per the reports above on this thread it does not resolve it in practice, and #53101 — the follow-up cherry-pick of `crrev.com/c/8272040` ("Use separate D-Bus connections for status icons") — is still open. So 43.2.0 appears to be the only shipping 43.x with a working Linux tray.

## Reproduction without a GUI

With any affected app running:

1. `gdbus call --session --dest org.freedesktop.DBus --object-path /org/freedesktop/DBus --method org.freedesktop.DBus.ListNames | tr ',' '\n' | grep StatusNotifierItem`
2. Read a property via that well-known name — succeeds.
3. `... --method org.freedesktop.DBus.GetNameOwner <well-known-name>` → `:1.NNN`
4. Repeat step 2 against `:1.NNN` — errors.

Steps 2 and 4 are the whole thing; the asymmetry between them is the bug.

Credit for the Cinnamon/X11 measurements, the concurrent 28-vs-43 comparison and the watcher logs: a user of my app who investigated the regression on his own machine.

Another affected host: **xfce4-panel 4.20.7** (Xfce 4.20, X11, Ubuntu 26.04). Adding it since the thread so far covers GNOME's appindicator extension, Cinnamon's `xapp-sn-watcher` and Unity — same failing path, the panel's Status Tray plugin is itself the `StatusNotifierWatcher` and resolves the registered name to its unique owner before reading properties.

Slack 4.51.191 (Electron 43.4.0) broken, 4.51.180 (Electron 43.1.1) works, matching @yannroux's Cinnamon report.

**The panel treats the first failed read as fatal and never retries** (`PANEL_DEBUG=systray`):

```
xfce4-panel(systray): ../plugins/systray/sn-item.c:699: Fatal error for item '(null)':
  (domain 'g-dbus-error-quark', code 0)
  GDBus.Error:org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.Failed: error occurred in GetAll
```

The item is registered and `Active` — it is dropped purely on the `GetAll` error, and re-registration on panel restart just reproduces it.

**There is no host-side workaround on Xfce.** I removed the Status Tray plugin so `ayatana-indicator-application-service` 22.2.0 would take `org.kde.StatusNotifierWatcher` instead. It resolves to the unique name too and fails identically:

```
method call sender=:1.2307 -> destination=:1.2322 path=/StatusNotifierItem;
  interface=org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties; member=GetAll
  string "org.kde.StatusNotifierItem"
error sender=:1.2322 -> destination=:1.2307 error_name=org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.Failed
  string "error occurred in GetAll"
```

So both tray hosts available on Xfce are on the failing path and swapping between them is not a mitigation — pinning Electron is the only option here.

One small thing that may save someone a detour: this is not a startup race. 1881 `GetAll` calls to the well-known name, issued in a loop across a panel restart, all succeeded — including ones landing in the same millisecond as the panel's failing call to the unique name.

only reports two other applications:

```text
as 2 "org.kde.StatusNotifierItem-2448-1/StatusNotifierItem" "org.kde.StatusNotifierItem-proton.vpn.app.gtk-2413/StatusNotifierItem"
```

So Plasma's StatusNotifierWatcher itself appears to be working; Vesktop simply never gets registered.

I also tested forcing Vesktop through X11/XWayland with:

```bash
vesktop --ozone-platform=x11
```

but the behavior is unchanged: no tray icon and no additional StatusNotifierItem is registered.

This seems consistent with #53024, which was closed as a duplicate of this issue and also reproduces the problem when using an external Electron 43.4.1 executable.

I can confirm this same regression manifests outside GNOME/Wayland too — on **Linux Mint 22.3 (Cinnamon 6.6.9)**, affecting **both Slack Desktop 4.51.191** and **Lens Desktop**, both bundling **Electron 43.4.0** (`Chrome/150.0.7871.224`). Both apps show a generic/broken tray icon glyph in Cinnamon's XApp Status Applet, and clicking them does nothing.

**Reproduction:**

Cinnamon's tray watcher (`xapp-sn-watcher`) logs this in `~/.xsession-errors` the moment either app starts:
```
** (xapp-sn-watcher:3122): CRITICAL **: Could not get properties for org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-<pid>-1: GDBus.Error:org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.Failed: error occurred in GetAll
```

I reproduced this manually. Calling `Properties.GetAll` with an **explicit interface name** succeeds and returns the full property set (icon pixmap, menu path, tooltip, etc.):
```
$ dbus-send --session --print-reply --dest=org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-<pid>-1 \
    /StatusNotifierItem org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties.GetAll \
    string:org.kde.StatusNotifierItem
# → succeeds, full property set returned
```

But calling it with an **empty interface string** (`''`) — which is what `GDBusProxy`-based watchers issue internally — fails identically to the watcher's error:
```
$ gdbus call --session --dest org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-<pid>-1 \
    --object-path /StatusNotifierItem \
    --method org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties.GetAll ''
Error: GDBus.Error:org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.Failed: error occurred in GetAll
```

This confirms the defect is in the app's own D-Bus property server (which changed with Electron 43.3's switch to well-known SNI bus names, `org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-PID-N`), not in the desktop environment. I also confirmed neither app loads `libappindicator`/`libayatana-appindicator3` at all (checked via `/proc/<pid>/maps`) — both implement the SNI D-Bus service directly via `libdbus-1`, so appindicator-lib installs/symlinks (a common suggested fix) are irrelevant here.

This looks like the same root cause described in Alexays/Waybar#5240: `GDBusProxy`-based clients that rely on cached/empty-interface property fetches get nothing back from the new well-known-name SNI object, while explicit-interface raw D-Bus calls still work fine.

Happy to test a patched Electron build or provide further traces if useful.
I can confirm the same issue than @vitalii-morvaniuk-airslate in Ubuntu 24.04
The issue is fixed in next release ( #53214, #53215 )

Does someone know how long since a 44.0.1+ or 43.4.2+ containing the tray fix is published ?

After updating to Slack 4.52.155, minimizing the window hides it completely: it leaves the taskbar and no tray icon is shown. Sound notifications still work, so the process is running, but there is no way to restore the window except killing Slack and starting it again.

This started on 2026-09-08 after Slack 4.52.155 and Plasma 6.7.4-2 updates.

Environment

Slack RPM: 4.52.155-0.1.el8 (official Slack repo), Electron/Chrome 44.0.0
Fedora Linux 44, kernel 7.1.13-200.fc44.x86_64
KDE Plasma 6.7.4-2, KWin 6.7.4-2, Qt 6.11.2, session: Wayland
GPU: Intel Iris Xe + NVIDIA GA107M (driver 610.57.04)
What happens

Open Slack, window is visible.
Minimize.
Window is gone from the taskbar and from the system tray. Slack keeps running (runFromTray).
Message sounds still play.
Technical notes

Process runs native Wayland (--ozone-platform=wayland).
A StatusNotifierItem is registered: org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-<pid>-1 at /org/chromium/StatusNotifierItem/1.
Introspection of that object returns an empty node; Activate / property getters fail (UnknownMethod). Plasma therefore has a dead tray slot and Slack has already hidden the window.
Workaround that restores minimize-to-taskbar: launch with --ozone-platform=x11 (not using it; waiting for a Slack/Electron fix).
This matches the Electron Linux tray/SNI regression (electron#52674) and KDE bug 524697. Please bundle an Electron build that includes the Chromium StatusNotifierItem fix.
@iovcho either upgrade to  44.2.0 or downgrade to  43.4.1.
Slack 4.52.155 bundles Electron 44.0.0. I can’t change the runtime; waiting for Slack to ship ≥ 44.2.0.

Well, you can. ArchLinux commonly does this.

Have a look:

https://aur.archlinux.org/packages/slack-electron

I hit the same issue with Slack 4.52.155 on Arch Linux, KDE Plasma 6.7.4, Wayland. Slack bundles Electron 44.0.0.

Slack was running with `runFromTray` enabled, but its icon was missing. Its D-Bus name existed, while `/StatusNotifierItem` exposed no interfaces. Restarting Slack and switching to X11 didn’t help.

Launching Slack with the already-installed Electron 43.6.0 restored the tray registration:

```bash
# Fully quit Slack first
electron43 /usr/lib/slack/resources/app.asar --gtk-version=3 -s
```

KDE then reported `Slack_status_icon_1` as `Active`, with valid icon image data.

To keep the workaround, I copied `/usr/share/applications/slack.desktop` to `~/.local/share/applications/slack.desktop` and changed its `Exec` line to:

```ini
Exec=/usr/bin/electron43 /usr/lib/slack/resources/app.asar --gtk-version=3 -s %U
```

This is a local workaround using a separate Electron runtime. Paths may differ on other distributions. Once Slack bundles the fix, the launcher override can be removed.

nodes.title: BaseWindow.setBounds throws an exception if some of the properties of the `Rectangle` are missing
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

43.1.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

MacOS 27 (Golden Gate)

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

unknown

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

[Documentation](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/api/base-window#winsetboundsbounds-animate) states that `BaseWindow::setBounds` accept `Partial<Rectangle>`.

This slightly modified example from docs should not throw any exceptions:

```ts
const { app, BaseWindow } = require('electron')

app.whenReady().then(() => {
  const win = new BaseWindow()

  // set all bounds properties
  win.setBounds({ x: 440, y: 225, width: 800, height: 600 })

  // set a single bounds property
  win.setBounds({ width: 100 })

  // { x: 440, y: 225, width: 100, height: 600 }
  console.log(win.getBounds())
})
```

### Actual Behavior

The provided example throws `UnhandledPromiseRejectionWarning: TypeError: Error processing argument at index 0`.



### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

Note, that it does not throw if I use `BrowserWindow` instead of `BaseWindow`.

This seems to be just an imperfection in documentation. Instead of saying the method accepts a `Partial<Rectangle>` we can tell it accepts a `Rectangle`.

`BrowserWindow` does not throw because it first fetches the current bounds before calling the method implemented in C++ code:

- https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/lib/browser/api/browser-window.ts#L23-L30

Alternatively, we can add the same wrapper to `BaseWindow`. I'll leave the decision to Electron maintainers. I'd tell if I it was up to me to decide, I would choose updating documentation and to not execute some `getBounds -> setBounds` code which is very likely not needed by app authors. If it was needed, the current bug report would be reported earlier than now 🙂

I think it would be best to match the `BrowserWindow` behavior.

Best if we can share the code and if we can call `getBounds()` only if properties are actually missing.

fixed by #54333, which moves the partial-bounds merge into `BaseWindow.setBounds()` natively so `baseWindow.setBounds({ width })` works as documented. it's on main (46) with a 45 backport pending. closing this out.
